_comment: AWS pricing rates (us-east-1, USD) for the estimate phase, sourced from the upstream pricing-cache.md. KNOWLEDGE per docs/unit-taxonomy-spec.md — rates evolve on AWS's cadence, independent of the cost algorithm. The cost FORMULAS and the per-service MULTI-AZ CONVENTION live here as data so the procedure does a lookup, not a guess. Output SHAPE is schemas/estimation-infra.schema.json.

_meta.staleness_note: If more than staleness_days past last_updated, infrastructure rates remain reliable; set pricing_source=cached_stale and note it. AI-model rates (not used for heroku->aws) may have drifted.

_multi_az_convention._comment: THE TRAP (see test-output/estimate-arithmetic-probe.md): a design's multi_az:true means different things per service. Each service rate below carries multi_az_handling so the formula applies the RIGHT adjustment, never a blanket multiplier.
_multi_az_convention.baked_in: rate already INCLUDES multi-AZ; NEVER apply a multiplier (multi_az flag is informational)
_multi_az_convention.multiplier_x2: rate is single-AZ; multiply by 2 when design multi_az == true
_multi_az_convention.intrinsic: service is inherently multi-AZ; no adjustment; multi_az flag informational

fargate.multi_az_handling: n/a (Fargate cost is task-size driven, not AZ-driven)

rds_postgresql._note: pricing-cache RDS PostgreSQL table is labeled (On-Demand, Multi-AZ) — the rate ALREADY includes multi-AZ. Do NOT double for multi_az.

aurora_postgresql._note: Aurora replicates across 3 AZs by default; rate is as-listed, no multi-AZ adjustment.
aurora_postgresql._instances_note: r6g.16xlarge extrapolated 2x from 8xlarge; verify via MCP if it drives a large estimate.
aurora_postgresql.formula: instance_rate * hours_per_month + storage_gb * storage_per_gb_month + io_estimate (io optional; default 0 absent usage data)

elasticache._note: pricing-cache ElastiCache is Single-AZ; apply x2 when design multi_az == true.
elasticache._nodes_note: m6g sizes above large extrapolated by doubling; verify via MCP if large.
elasticache.formula: node_rate * hours_per_month * (2 if design multi_az else 1)

msk._note: broker_count already spans AZs (2 or 3 per design); cost is per-broker, no extra multi-AZ multiplier.
msk._brokers_note: MSK broker rates approximate; verify via MCP for a kafka-heavy estimate.
msk.formula: broker_rate * hours_per_month * broker_count + storage_per_broker_gb * broker_count * storage_per_gb_month

eks._comment: EKS cost = control plane (once) + EC2 nodes; PODS COST $0 (compute billed via nodes — charging pods double-counts). Post-loop add, gated on an eks_cluster design entry. EKS-aware now though design's EKS branch is a stub.
eks.formula: control_plane_monthly + node_monthly_rate * node_count  (+ ALB per web service + NAT if private subnets). Per-pod Fargate-style task cost is NOT charged.

nat_gateway.formula: monthly_fixed (+ per_gb_processed * data_gb estimate; default data 0 absent usage)

rds_proxy.formula: per_vcpu_hour * hours_per_month * vcpus (when connection pooling mapped)

ses.formula: flat minimal baseline from SendGrid mapping

amazon_mq.formula: instance_rate * 730 + storage (CloudAMQP mapping; verify via MCP)

opensearch.formula: instance_rate * 730 + storage (Bonsai mapping; verify via MCP)

elasticache_memcached._use: same node rates as elasticache (Memcachier mapping)
